speaker: Doctor
text: That is a very helpful start; can you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and if they have changed in size or color? Do you or anyone else notice itching, pain, or fever accompanying them?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the daycare exposure and recent chickenpox in the household, could you tell me if these lesions are vesicular or crusty, and do they follow a rash distribution typical of a specific virus like varicella or molluscum? Also, has the child had any fever or lethargy?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum. The description of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is pathognomonic for this viral infection, especially given the daycare exposure. No further tests are required at this time.
